correctness.rationale: For a nonclosed support U, choose points in U converging geometrically to a boundary point in F and pairwise disjoint bump functions supported inside U. Disjoint synthesis gives an isometric lattice embedding of c0, while evaluation at the convergent points maps I_F contractively to c0 and composes to the identity. Published retract permanence and c0 non-semiprojectivity then rule out semiprojectivity. If U is clopen, extension by zero identifies I_F isometrically with C(U), so the published C(Y)-ANR theorem gives the positive classification. The standard closed-ideal correspondence completes the proof.

evidence: The C(Y) theorem covers compact supports once they are clopen but says nothing by itself about nonclosed open supports of ideals.
The new retract construction supplies the missing negative half.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves an explicit open Cantor-ideal case in the defining recent paper and gives a complete topological classification of all closed ideals of C(X), with a reusable boundary-support obstruction.
residual_risks: The disjoint-bump retract is elementary and may have antecedents in general C0(U) Banach-lattice theory, though no implication-equivalent semiprojectivity result was located.

final_claim: For compact metric X, a closed lattice ideal of C(X) is semiprojective exactly when it is zero or is supported on a nonempty clopen ANR; every nonclosed open support contains c0 as a contractive lattice retract, so in particular the Cantor-set ideal in C([0,1]) is not semiprojective.
limitations: Compact metric X and closed lattice ideals only.
No general extension-permanence theorem is claimed.
